speaker: amari_ndlovu
headline: DIGNITY MUST SURVIVE THE JOURNEY.
deck: A right is weakened when people are recognised at the policy level but disappear at the next administrative handoff.
quote: Recognition is not a ceremonial word. It must remain visible from the first promise to the final encounter.
facts: Access begins with being seen as a full participant.
Language and place affect whether a service can be used.
Repeated exclusion accumulates as institutional memory.
The final handoff determines whether dignity becomes material.
takeaway: A system protects dignity only when recognition survives every handoff.
